solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wife, a female surreptitious and vague

parts.note: fly in British slang means sly, cunning, quietly knowing

explanation.surface: A sneaky wife who keeps her answers deliberately fuzzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Waffly talk rambles without saying anything definite, so it is imprecise and woolly.

clue.text: Enemy of distracted knight — mind will wander

indicators.note: letters that wander stray from their places, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight so distracted that his mind and will drift off.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight is Don Quixote, Cervantes's deluded hero, who charged at windmills thinking they were giants.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote, the crazed knight of Cervantes, famously attacked these sail-driven mills as foes.

clue.text: Novels etc about end of war and conflict

indicators.note: the novels word goes about, around, the other letter

parts.note: novels and the like are fiction

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of war

explanation.surface: War novels and similar books, dealing with the end of a war and its strife.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is discord or clashing between people, a synonym for conflict.

clue.text: Willingly tell porkies with frequency

parts.note: porkies (from pork pies, Cockney rhyming slang for lies) are lies, so to tell them is to lie
F is the physics abbreviation for frequency

explanation.surface: Someone happily and often telling fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porkies' is British slang for lies, from the rhyming slang 'pork pies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lief is an archaic adverb meaning gladly, as in 'I would as lief stay'.

clue.text: Mistake concerning wardrobe item

parts.note: a slip is a small error
over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: An error involving something in the wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipover is a sleeveless pullover, a piece of clothing kept in a wardrobe.

clue.text: Rare wet idler working as a journalist

indicators.note: working implies the letters are being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rarely seen lazy wimp who is actually employed in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British slang for feeble or ineffectual.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader writer composes a newspaper's editorials, so is a kind of newspaper writer.

clue.text: The old man getting ill cannot thank you for creamy dish

parts.note: the old man is a familiar term for father, PA

indicators.note: ill, meaning badly, signals that the word cannot is put into bad order

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Father feels unwell and can't say thanks for his pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Panna cotta is an Italian dessert of set sweetened cream.

clue.text: I've worried about food?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the food word
worried in the sense of shaken about, so the letters of the word are disturbed

parts.note: an egg is an item of food

explanation.surface: Someone fretting over what to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue is also the plaintive cry of a fussy eater, which is what makes it an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Veggie is informal for vegetarian, someone who has to think carefully about what they eat.

clue.text: Dish with eggs needing whisk? Not right

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: not right means the R, right, is taken away

parts.note: to whisk is to stir

explanation.surface: A recipe of eggs that calls for whisking, apparently wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of fried grated potato.

clue.text: One has snooped around, it's rumoured

indicators.note: the snooping word is placed around the numeral

parts.note: to nose is to pry or snoop
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone has been prying and the gossip is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Noised, as in noised abroad, means spread about as talk or gossip.

clue.text: Philanthropist of nicer age possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could form something else

explanation.surface: A benefactor from a kinder era.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Carnegie, the steel magnate, gave away a vast fortune to libraries and causes.

clue.text: Boss given four bits of news in central office

parts.note: the head is the boss
N, E, W and S are the four quarters of the compass, so the bits of news are quarters

explanation.surface: A boss handed four snippets of news at head office.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWS spells the four compass points, which are also called quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Headquarters is the main administrative office of an organisation.

clue.text: Mum falling short as a partner

indicators.note: falling short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for mother

explanation.surface: A mother who doesn't quite make it as a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a partner, whether spouse, companion or breeding partner.

clue.text: Type of scholar with information taking time to catalogue

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
an era is a period of time
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A scholar armed with data spending time drawing up a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A generalist has broad knowledge across many fields rather than a specialism.

clue.text: Commercial cleaner — last bit of scum it removed

indicators.note: read as re-moved, moved again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the last bit of scum is its final letter, M, and the word it follows as written

explanation.surface: A cleaning product that took the scum off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed', read as moved again, rearranges CLEANER with M (the last letter of scum) and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile means relating to trade and merchants, so commercial.

clue.text: From the extraterrestrial's perspective our planet may be viewed with contempt!

definitions.text: From the extraterrestrial's perspective our planet may be viewed with contempt!

parts.words: From the extraterrestrial's perspective our planet may be viewed with contempt
parts.note: an alien hovering in space literally gazes downward at Earth, and the phrase also means regarded as inferior

explanation.surface: Aliens holding Earth in disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: To be looked down on is to be scorned; from space, Earth is also physically below the viewer.

clue.text: Report of people stealing clothes-line items?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to nick is British slang for steal, so thieves are nickers

explanation.surface: News of thieves pinching the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's underpants, the sort of thing pegged out on a washing line.

clue.text: Broadcaster Kate among all others is best prepared

indicators.note: the broadcaster goes among, inside, the others

parts.note: the rest means all the others
Kate Adie is a well-known BBC news correspondent

explanation.surface: A newscaster outshining everyone else in readiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Adie is a famous BBC war correspondent.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiest is the superlative of ready, meaning most prepared.

clue.text: An opportunity hotel missed to incorporate charming familiarity

parts.note: an becomes the article A

indicators.note: the shortened word takes in, incorporates, the charming word
missed means the hotel letter is left out

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
quaint means attractively old-fashioned, charming

explanation.surface: A chance missed at a hotel to include some charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' drops H from CHANCE, giving CANCE, which then takes in QUAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquaintance with a subject is knowledge of it, a familiarity.

clue.text: Heavenly dwelling in senorita's garden

indicators.note: in signals the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Paradise found in a Spanish lady's garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Asgard is the home of the gods in Norse mythology.

clue.text: Maiden in alternatives to stockings and dresses

indicators.note: the maiden letter goes in the hosiery word

parts.note: socks are worn instead of stockings
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl choosing between socks, stockings and frocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocks are loose dresses or overgarments.

clue.text: Schools offering a number of regular programmes carrying weight in Greece

indicators.note: the programmes word carries, contains, the weight

parts.note: a series is a run of regular broadcast programmes
a mina was an ancient Greek unit of weight

explanation.surface: Schools broadcasting shows that include heavy Greek content.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminaries are colleges, especially for training priests.

clue.text: Fish in burn having abandoned lake

indicators.note: having abandoned means the lake letter is dropped

parts.note: a scald is a burn from hot liquid
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fish found in a burn, which in Scotland is a stream, having left the loch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is a Scottish word for a stream, but here it means a scald.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a fish, also called horse mackerel.

clue.text: Not all choir turning up — three performers only

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
not all of the words are used, only some letters inside them

explanation.surface: Only three singers in the choir show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' takes OIRT from 'choir turning' and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three musicians.

clue.text: Knife carried by a revolutionary is put in store

indicators.note: the knife is carried inside the revolutionary word

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
a chiv is a slang word for a knife

explanation.surface: A rebel's blade is locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Archived records are filed away in a repository for safekeeping.

clue.text: Author wildly energetic twitching away

indicators.note: wildly means the letters are thrown into disorder
away means some letters go out of the word before the rest are rearranged

parts.note: a tic is a twitching of the muscles

explanation.surface: A writer full of wild energy, twitching uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TIC out of ENERGETIC and rearrange the remaining ENERGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was the English novelist of Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.

clue.text: Pass out as girl with discernment, keeping quiet

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the discernment word keeps the quiet letter inside

parts.note: sense is good judgement, discernment
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A sensible girl handing things out in silence.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or hand out.

clue.text: Conservative county in which leader's denied support

indicators.note: the first letter of the county is refused, removed

parts.note: Dorset is a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A Tory county where the top man won't back anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a tight undergarment that supports the body.
